statement: Annotated from the Beinecke scan alone (full page, three horizontal strips and a zoom on the label area); no transcription word and no other annotation of this folio was read. The page is a pharmaceutical page in two registers. The upper register holds a red lidded jar at the left margin and ten whole plants in two rows: five across the top (broad-lobed, a thick looped stem, a tall pinnate plant, a small lobed plant, and a spiky plant with two blue flowers and a red root) and five across the second row (broad leaves with a red root, a spiky rosette around a pale centre, a spiky plant with red root, a single tall triangular leaf on a red root, and a round-leaved plant), plus a large two-leaf plant at the right edge. A paragraph follows. The lower register holds a second red lidded jar at the left margin and five whole plants: a tall spiky plant with a deep red taproot, a small tree-like plant, a single teardrop leaf on an arched stem, a round bushy plant, and a large serrated plant with red roots. A second paragraph follows. Label loci were read from the transcription's line ids and unit codes only, and paired with objects by the labels' positions on the page: the eleven upper-register label lines fall in order down the page, the five written above objects (f100r.1 to f100r.5) name the five top-row plants left to right, then f100r.6 names the large two-leaf plant at the upper right, and f100r.7 to f100r.11 name the second-row plants left to right from their labels below. In the lower register f100r.16 names the tall spiky plant (its label stands above it); the remaining lower label lines stand together at the bases of the row and are left unassigned rather than guessed. Both jars carry no label line and are recorded with label null.
